assumptions: This is a model output, not an observed fact. It estimates what the valuation appears to require; it does not state what the company will do.
Market inputs are as of 2026-09-27: about $1.47T market cap at about $372 per share, trailing P/E near 386.
Fundamentals are Tesla 10-K figures: FY2025 revenue $94.8B, net income $3.8B, and two straight years of falling vehicle deliveries.
Embedded expectations are inferred from the gap between price and fundamentals, not stated by the company.

embeddedExpectations.assumption: Current fleet is under 500 registered vehicles in Texas; autonomy is unsolved.
Still in the R&D phase per Musk on the January 2026 earnings call; contributes no revenue.
Deliveries fell in both 2024 and 2025; lineup is aging and competition is rising.
46.7 GWh in 2025 with strong margins; the one segment already delivering.
embeddedExpectations.outcome: Energy storage keeps compounding at high rates

expectationGap.gapSummary: At about $1.47T against $3.8B of trailing net income, the valuation prices in outcomes far beyond the current business: two straight years of falling deliveries, thin and shrinking auto margins, and one growing energy segment. The distance between demonstrated business substance and the future story required by the price is the expectation gap.
